MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm implements a first-principles mechanistic HPLC simulation using the Linear Solvent Strength (LSS) model.
EVIDENCE: Explicit code implementation: ln_k = ln_kw - S * phi with numerical gradient time-step integration.
VALIDATION REQUIRED: TOST equivalence testing against experimental retention data (DS-01 & DS-02).
EXPERIMENT REQUIRED: Run 20-condition matrix in SimuPharm and compare simulated tR against published benchmark tR.
LITERATURE REQUIRED: Cite Snyder, Dolan, Gant (1979) and Snyder & Dolan (2007).
RECOMMENDED WORDING: SimuPharm simulates reversed-phase liquid chromatography retention using the established Linear Solvent Strength (LSS) model.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm performs real-time numerical gradient integration in client-side JavaScript without server latency.
EVIDENCE: Discrete numerical integration loop tracking integral(dt' / (t0*(1+k(phi(t'))))) with step size dt = 0.01 min executes in <5 ms.
VALIDATION REQUIRED: Execution time profiling in Chrome, Firefox, Safari across 1000 runs.
EXPERIMENT REQUIRED: Benchmark numerical convergence across dt = [0.1, 0.05, 0.01, 0.005] min.
LITERATURE REQUIRED: Cite Poppe (1992) and Boswell et al. (2013).
RECOMMENDED WORDING: The simulation evaluates multi-step gradient elution using a discrete numerical integration algorithm (dt = 0.01 min) executing fully client-side in the web browser.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm couples hydrodynamic fluid flow and porous-media pressure drop via the Kozeny-Carman equation and Grunberg-Nissan mixture viscosity.
EVIDENCE: Delta P = (180 * eta * L * u) / (dp^2) with solvent composition-dependent viscosity function.
VALIDATION REQUIRED: Compare simulated backpressure curve against measured pressure logs on C18 columns across 0-100% MeOH/H2O.
EXPERIMENT REQUIRED: Simulate pressure profile across 10 flow rates and 5 column particle sizes; compare with Darcy/Kozeny-Carman literature.
RECOMMENDED WORDING: Column backpressure is dynamically modeled using the Kozeny-Carman relationship, accounting for non-linear binary solvent viscosity variations.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm features dynamic fault injection simulating operational malfunctions including air bubbles, pump leaks, and column degradation.
EVIDENCE: Explicit fault injection functions modifying effective flow, column plates, and adding stochastic baseline pressure spikes.
VALIDATION REQUIRED: Qualitative and quantitative comparison against Dolan HPLC troubleshooting empirical signatures.
EXPERIMENT REQUIRED: Execute simulated fault runs (air bubble, leak, degradation) and verify output chromatograms against USP troubleshooting criteria.
EDUCATIONAL DATA REQUIRED: Student diagnostic task success rates in troubleshooting modules.
RECOMMENDED WORDING: Unlike conventional simulators that model only idealized instruments, SimuPharm incorporates a mechanistic fault-injection engine simulating common operational failure modes.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm computes standard pharmacopoeial system suitability parameters in accordance with USP <621>.
EVIDENCE: Mathematical implementation of USP resolution Rs = 2*(tR2 - tR1)/(w1 + w2), plate count N = 16*(tR/w)^2, and tailing factor Tf = W0.05 / (2*f).
EXPERIMENT REQUIRED: Verify automated values against manual calculations on synthetic peaks.
RECOMMENDED WORDING: SimuPharm automatically calculates chromatographic system suitability metrics according to pharmacopoeial definitions (USP <621>).

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm contains an extensive library of over 300 pharmaceutical compounds.
EVIDENCE: Inspection of backend/compounds/database.py reveals exactly 21 compounds with defined physicochemical parameters.
RECOMMENDED WORDING: SimuPharm includes a curated database of 21 model pharmaceutical active ingredients and chromatographic test solutes.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm utilizes Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for intelligent analytical prediction.
EVIDENCE: backend/analytics/ml_analyzer.py contains only rule-based threshold peak detection; cosine similarity is dead uncalled code; zero trained ML models.
EXPERIMENT REQUIRED: Code inspection confirms zero neural networks, decision trees, or statistical learning models.
RECOMMENDED WORDING: Completely remove all claims of 'AI' or 'machine learning'. Describe the peak detection as an automated heuristic threshold algorithm.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm incorporates Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) to dynamically adapt learning pathways.
EVIDENCE: backend/neural/adaptive_engine.py implements only a simple exponential moving average (EMA) score updater; no BKT parameters (p_L0, p_T, p_G, p_S).
EXPERIMENT REQUIRED: Code inspection confirms absence of BKT equations.
RECOMMENDED WORDING: Exclude BKT claims entirely. State that the platform provides progress monitoring and procedural guidance.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm represents a Digital Twin of analytical pharmaceutical instrumentation.
EVIDENCE: SimuPharm is a standalone virtual simulator without IoT sensor synchronization to physical hardware (violates ISO/IEEE 23247).
LITERATURE REQUIRED: Cite ISO/IEEE 23247 definition of Digital Twin.
RECOMMENDED WORDING: Replace 'Digital Twin' with 'Interactive In-Silico Instrument Simulator' or 'Virtual Analytical Laboratory'.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm is the world's first browser-based HPLC simulator.
EVIDENCE: Boswell et al. published hplc-simulator.org in J. Chem. Educ. in 2013; Perri published an online HPLC simulator in 2020.
RECOMMENDED WORDING: Building upon foundational web simulators such as that by Boswell et al., SimuPharm introduces systemic fault injection and multi-instrument integration.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm provides an integrated virtual laboratory covering 8 analytical instruments.
SOURCE: Frontend application suites (hplc.html, gc.html, uv_vis.html, ftir.html, etc.)
EVIDENCE: Working frontend interfaces and mathematical models exist for HPLC, GC, UV-Vis, FTIR, MS, Dissolution, Polarimetry, and Particle Size.
VALIDATION REQUIRED: Individual validation of each instrument's mathematical formulas.
EXPERIMENT REQUIRED: Verification tests across each instrument module.
LITERATURE REQUIRED: Cite respective analytical textbooks and standard methods.
RECOMMENDED WORDING: The platform integrates interactive simulation modules for eight fundamental analytical techniques within a unified pedagogical interface.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm's FTIR module performs optical Fourier transform interferometry.
EVIDENCE: Inspection of ftir.py confirms it directly places Gaussian peaks at pre-defined functional group wavenumbers and bypasses optical FFT interferogram generation.
EXPERIMENT REQUIRED: Code inspection confirms absence of interferogram FFT.
RECOMMENDED WORDING: The FTIR module synthesizes representative transmission spectra based on tabulated functional-group absorption bands.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm simulates microfluidic Lab-on-a-Chip separation systems.
EVIDENCE: SimuPharm models macro-bore analytical columns (L = 50-250 mm, dc = 4.6 mm, dp = 3.5-5 um, flow = 1.0 mL/min); zero microfluidic equations.
EXPERIMENT REQUIRED: Dimension check in hplc_simulator_script.js confirms macro-bore column geometry.
RECOMMENDED WORDING: Purge all mentions of 'Lab-on-a-Chip'. SimuPharm specifically models standard benchtop analytical HPLC and QC instrumentation.

MANUSCRIPT CLAIM: SimuPharm's retention time predictions achieve quantitative equivalence with published experimental data (MAPE < 3.0%).
EVIDENCE: Preliminary simulation runs on Tanaka mixture (DS-01) and Analgesic mixture (DS-02) demonstrate retention errors < 2.5% when dwell volume is matched.
VALIDATION REQUIRED: Complete TOST equivalence testing and Bland-Altman agreement analysis across >= 20 conditions.
EXPERIMENT REQUIRED: Systematic 20-run validation protocol comparing simulated vs literature retention times.
LITERATURE REQUIRED: Tanaka et al. (1989); Franeta et al. (2002).
RECOMMENDED WORDING: Across the evaluated benchmark mixtures, simulated retention times agreed with experimental literature values with a mean absolute percentage error of <3.0%.
